set.why_biologic: Two segments. (1) Lateral/posterolateral transfixing implants (SI-BONE iFuse, iFuse-3D, iFuse TORQ, iFuse Bedrock Granite; Globus SI-LOK/SI-LOK SELECT; Orthofix FIREBIRD SI; Medtronic Rialto, K251395 2025; Camber Siconus; Spinal Simplicity Liberty-SI; Aurora SiLO TFX, K221047; CornerLoc TransLoc 3D, K232878; Tenon Catamaran; Tenon SImmetry+) are 510(k) titanium devices whose fusion claim rests on porous/coated surfaces and, in the fenestrated screws, bone that the implant self-harvests through its flutes (iFuse-3D 'fenestrated design to self-harvest bone'; FIREBIRD 'radial fenestrations allow self-harvesting of autograft'; SI-LOK 'optional graft slot'; Rialto IFU 'autograft and/or allograft may be placed in conjunction'). The INSITE, iMIA and SALLY trials of iFuse used no added graft. None of these vendors' product pages names a cellular allograft or DBM for the SI joint, so biologic use with transfixing screws is surgeon-discretionary and unbranded. (2) Posterior intra-articular 'fusion' implants ARE the biologic: machined structural cortical allograft dowels or spacers placed into the decorticated joint, regulated as 361 HCT/Ps (homologous use) rather than cleared devices. Products: PainTEQ LinQ (and the cortical-piercing TRAQ), SI-BONE iFuse INTRA V/INTRA X (supplied by an undisclosed third-party tissue bank), Aurora Spine SiLO, CornerLoc grafts (cortical graft plus a DBM sponge), Omnia Medical PsiF allograft, Vyrsa Pro (Vyrsa -> Nevro 2023 -> Globus 2025). Several are packed with DBM in a graft window at the surgeon's discretion. Titanium posterior 'in-line' implants (Camber SI, Spinal Simplicity Patriot-SI, CornerLoc TransLoc 3D posterior, Omnia PsiF DNA K-cleared May 2025, SI-BONE iFuse INTRA Ti) are moving the posterior approach back to 510(k) metal that must be paired with, or itself pierces, cortical bone.
set.autograft_standard: No iliac crest is harvested in MIS SI fusion. For transfixing screws the 'autograft' is local bone self-harvested by the fenestrated implant; for posterior allograft systems the graft is the implant itself (structural cortical allograft, optionally with DBM in the window). Open SI arthrodesis historically used iliac crest from the adjacent ilium.
set.volume_note: Medicare fee-for-service: 33,963 SI joint fusions 2010-2020, rising from 318 (2010) to 7,794 (2020); 68.5% MIS (CPT 27279) since 2015 (Federico 2023, PMID 37192412). SI-BONE FY2025 10-K: 'over 140,000 procedures have been performed using our products since we introduced iFuse in 2009' (as of 31 Dec 2025); 2025 revenue $200.9M (+20.2%), US $191.1M, international $9.8M, gross margin 79.6%. Aurora Spine reported >2,500 SiLO procedures (June 2025 release). No public procedure count for LinQ, CornerLoc, PsiF or Vyrsa.
set.coverage_note: CPT: 27279 (lateral/transfixing, since 2015; device-intensive in ASC, 2026 CMS unadjusted ASC $14,518, HOPD APC 5116 $17,914) and 27278 (posterior intra-articular, no transfixation; Category I since 1 Jan 2024 replacing Category III 0775T, which existed 2022-2023; 2026 ASC $15,048, same APC 5116). For 2026 the AMA revised both descriptors: 27279 = transarticular and/or intra-articular device(s) piercing the ilium/sacrum cortices, 27278 = intra-articular device(s) without cortical piercing, so cortical-piercing posterior products (PainTEQ TRAQ, SI-BONE INTRA Ti) bill 27279 and hybrids (posterior in-line plus transfixing screw) bill 27279. Medicare physician fee 2026: 27279 $762; 27278 $441 facility / $13,834 office-based lab (SI-BONE 10-K). Inpatient (rare): ICD-10-PCS 0SG734Z/0SG834Z group to FY2026 MS-DRG 450/451 Single Level Spinal Fusion Except Cervical with/without MCC ($38,782 / $23,507 unadjusted; SI-BONE facility guide Feb 2026). Device C-codes C1889/C1776 are packaged (no separate payment). Medicare coverage: CGS (L39802, KY/OH), Noridian (L39810/L39812, JE/JF; JF retired 23 Oct 2025 into the JE policy) and Palmetto (L39797, JJ/JM) finalized LCDs effective 17 Apr 2025 (Noridian 16 Feb 2025) stating that MI arthrodesis of the SIJ 'WITHOUT placement of a transfixation device is NOT considered medically reasonable and necessary', i.e. 27278/posterior allograft is non-covered in those jurisdictions; the Noridian evidence review quotes ISASS that posterior MI SIJF is 'unproven and not recommended'. SI-BONE's 10-K says these LCDs 'precluding coverage for CPT 27278' reduced demand for INTRA X. NGS/Wellpoint (L36406, revised 1 Apr 2026) and WPS (L36000, rev. 27 Jun 2024) still describe the covered procedure as 'percutaneous insertion of a metallic device across the SIJ' without naming 27278; Novitas and First Coast have no SI fusion LCD that this pass could find. ACR, ASPN and NANS objected to the three 2025 LCDs; the LCDs stand as of Oct 2026. iFuse Bedrock Granite received hospital-outpatient/ASC transitional pass-through from 1 Jan 2025 and iFuse TORQ TNT an NTAP (hardware, not biologics).
set.nonunion_note: iFuse: INSITE RCT (n=148, SI-BONE sponsored, no added graft) 6-month success 81.4% surgical vs 26.1% nonsurgical; 3 revisions in 102 fusions at 24 months. SALLY (NCT03122899, iFuse-3D, n=51): independent CT bridging bone 77% at 12 months and 90% at 5 years (Patel 2020 PMID 32607011; Patel 2024 PMID 39344079); iMIA RCT (NCT01741025) CT at 12 months: radiolucency adjacent to 4.0% of implants (Dengler 2019 PMID 30845034). Posterior allograft: SECURE (LinQ, NCT04423120, n=122 implanted) reports composite responder 73.5% at 12 months with no CT fusion endpoint; the only CT-graded posterior series retrieved is SImmetry decortication-plus-graft (lateral), 94% bridging at 24 months. No independent fusion or nonunion rate for any posterior allograft product was found, which is the basis of the LCD non-coverage.

challenge: Products are now identified, but no posterior allograft vendor discloses its tissue bank (SI-BONE's 10-K says only 'a third-party' HCT/P manufacturer; PainTEQ's FAQ says 'treated, sterile bone'). The SI-BONE cumulative count is a company figure and the earlier 'nearly 150,000' (Q4 2025 release, IR site not fetchable) does not match the 10-K's 'over 140,000'; the 10-K figure is used. No cellular allograft or DBM brand could be tied to any SI system from a primary source, so Trinity/Osteocel 'with' FIREBIRD/SI-LOK remains unverified and is not paired.

new_record.name: LinQ SI Joint Stabilization System (and TRAQ)
new_record.composition: Machined structural cortical bone allograft ('almond-shaped' with a graft window), placed posteriorly into the decorticated mid-joint; TRAQ (2026) is a cortical-piercing allograft variant engaging sacral and iliac cortices at four points. Window may be packed with DBM at surgeon discretion (physician descriptions; not in the IFU text retrieved).

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: SECURE (NCT04423120; Calodney 2024, PMID 38524688): prospective single-arm, 16 US sites, 122 implanted, composite responder 73.5% at 12 months, one procedure-related SAE; no CT fusion endpoint. Bovinet 2025 (PMID 40832586): retrospective 6-site cohort n=258, NRS 7.6 to 1.6 at mean 1.75 years. Ampomah 2025 (PMID 40828365): n=260, AE 1.9% at 6 months. LINQT RCT vs conservative management (NCT07558278, n=200, started Jul 2026) is the first randomized trial of any posterior allograft.
applications.caveats: All clinical data are pain/function case series by interventional pain physicians with company involvement; no radiographic fusion rate; no comparison to lateral transfixing implants; three MAC LCDs (2025) non-cover procedures without a transfixation device.

evidence.title: SECURE: single-arm multicenter prospective study of LinQ
evidence.finding: 73.5% composite responders at 12 months; one procedure-related serious AE.

evidence.title: Safety, efficacy and durability of outcomes: results from SECURE
evidence.finding: VAS and ODI significantly improved at 12 months; responder rate stable 66-74% across visits.

evidence.title: Minimally invasive posterior SI joint fusion with a novel cortical allograft: real-world long-term outcomes, multisite US cohort
evidence.finding: Mean NRS reduction 6.0 points at 91 weeks; no serious AEs reported.

evidence.title: Retrospective evaluation of adverse events in posterior approach with bone allograft
evidence.finding: AE incidence 2.3% at 3 months and 1.9% at 6 months; no device-related events.

evidence.title: Multicenter retrospective analysis of a posterior sacroiliac fusion device (LinQ)
evidence.finding: NRS 6.98 to 3.06 at mean 612 days; no major AEs.

evidence.title: LINQT: open-label RCT of LinQ vs conventional medical management
evidence.finding: Enrolling; primary endpoint composite responder at 6 months, follow-up 24 months.

evidence.title: TRAQTION: post-market single-arm study of TRAQ

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: PainTEQ's clinician page states LinQ and TRAQ are HCT/Ps 'regulated solely under Section 361' and 'not FDA-cleared or FDA-approved medical devices'. PainTEQ drove the 0775T (2022) and 27278 (2024) code applications using SECURE interim data. Company ranked on Inc. 5000 (2024). Office-based-lab 27278 physician payment ($13,834 in 2026) is the economic engine for interventional pain practices.

new_record.ownership_history: PainTEQ (Tampa, FL) private; majority growth recapitalization co-led by Signet Healthcare Partners and Windham Capital Partners, Aug 2025.
new_record.challenge: Tissue bank that processes LinQ not disclosed in any public source retrieved; 'DBM packed in the window' comes from physician/trade descriptions, not the IFU.

new_record.name: iFuse INTRA V and iFuse INTRA X Allograft Implant Systems
new_record.composition: INTRA V (formerly INTRA): single triangular cortical allograft; INTRA X: two small cylindrical bone allografts; both 'implantable bone products manufactured from sterilized recovered cadaveric bone tissue', placed intra-articularly through a ~2 cm posterior incision.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical study retrieved; SI-BONE's product pages cite only finite-element analysis of SI joint motion and state the results are 'not necessarily indicative of human clinical results'. The FY2025 10-K attributes reduced INTRA X demand to the 2024-2025 MAC LCDs precluding coverage of CPT 27278.
applications.caveats: Launched 2024 as a defensive entry into the interventional-pain posterior segment; no SI-BONE-sponsored trial lists the allograft products (NCT07565545 is the titanium INTRA Ti). Manufactured and distributed as HCT/Ps by an undisclosed third-party tissue bank.

evidence.title: iFuse INTRA Ti (titanium posterior-inferior intra-articular cortical-piercing implant) safety and effectiveness
evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting (start Sep 2026); titanium successor billed under 27279, not the allograft.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: 10-K: 'Our iFuse INTRA/INTRA X implants are derived from human bone tissue ... manufactured and distributed by a third-party as HCT/P products'; 10-K maps INTRA X to CPT 27278 ($441 facility / $13,834 OBL physician fee 2026) and the titanium products to 27279. SI-BONE sells direct (89 territory managers, 83 clinical specialists, 320 agents, FY2025).

new_record.challenge: Tissue bank not named; no clinical data; the 2024 launch year comes from the 10-K product chronology, not a dated release.

new_record.name: SiLO Posterior SI-Fusion System (allograft)
new_record.composition: Single dowel of human cortical bone with three circumferential ridges ('Dowel Anchorage Design') and dual vertical side channels that accept additional bone graft during insertion; posterior intra-articular, non-transfixing. SiLO TFX (K221047, Oct 2022; titanium cone plus ilium and sacrum screws, graft placed in the barrel) is the company's 510(k) transfixing hybrid and is a device, not a biologic.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed clinical series for the SiLO allograft was retrieved; the company reported >2,500 SiLO procedures in the US (June 2025 release) and a cadaveric study of SiLO TFX. Aurora launched 'Aurora Biologics' in late 2025 to sell biologics with its implants.
applications.caveats: Company-reported volume only; SiLO TFX revenue grew 135% in 2024 and aggregate SI implant sales +8.4% in 2025 (press releases), implying the titanium hybrid, not the allograft, is the growth product after the 2025 LCDs.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Aurora Spine (TSXV: ASG / OTC: ASAPF), FY2025 revenue $18.4M (+4.6%); SI implants are one of three product lines. Distributor-based sales.

new_record.challenge: Tissue processor not disclosed; no clinical outcomes paper found for the allograft; SiLO vs SiLO TFX volumes not separated.

new_record.name: CornerLoc SI Joint Fusion grafts
new_record.composition: Two machined cortical bone allografts placed orthogonally into the prepared posterior joint through two small incisions, with a demineralized bone matrix sponge; non-transfixing. The company's TransLoc 3D (K232878, Oct 2023) is a 3D-printed titanium modular posterior implant plus lateral-oblique screws (hybrid) and is a device.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed clinical series of the allograft retrieved; physician and hospital pages (UK HealthCare) describe the technique and a 12-month ossification timeline. CornerLoc's registered studies (NCT05916092 SPARTAN n=240; NCT06487936 registry) cover the titanium TransLoc 3D.
applications.caveats: Company founded 2017 (Tulsa, OK); evidence for the graft product is descriptive only; the hybrid TransLoc 3D exists because the posterior allograft alone is non-covered under the 2025 LCDs.

evidence.title: SPARTAN: post-market study of TransLoc 3D screw-only vs hybrid constructs
evidence.finding: Company reports 91.7% improved in pain and function at 6 months (interim, unpublished).

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Private; sells surgery-ready trays to pain practices and ASCs. The DBM sponge is unbranded in all sources.

new_record.challenge: Tissue bank and the DBM brand are not disclosed; launch year inferred from the 2017 founding and 2018-2019 physician adoption, not a dated release.

new_record.name: PsiF Posterior SI Fusion allograft
new_record.composition: Structural allograft bone implant placed through a postero-inferior intra-articular trajectory into a decorticated channel in the articular joint, secured mortise-and-tenon in subchondral bone (Lynch 2022). PsiF DNA (510(k) May 2025, launched Jan 2026) is a titanium double-helix transfixing implant placed ilium-to-sacrum that is packed with graft and leverages self-harvested autograft; PsiFGuard (SpineGuard, K-cleared Oct 2024) is the drilling-guidance device.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: Lynch 2022 (PMID 36420375): 57-patient multicenter registry, back pain 6.8 to 3.8 at 6 months. Kaye 2024 (PMID 39087970): LSU Shreveport single-center series of 72 posterior fusions (83% LinQ, remainder PsiF), VAS -3.6 cm, no procedure-related AEs, 54% with one-year follow-up. Latif 2023 (PMID 37511749) is a technique paper for PsiF DNA.
applications.caveats: Small registries with company-affiliated authors; PsiF results are pooled with LinQ in the only independent series; no fusion imaging endpoint.

evidence.title: Minimally invasive inferior intra-articular SI joint fusion with allograft bone
evidence.finding: Back pain 6.8 to 3.8 at 6 months; all outcomes p<0.001; no fusion endpoint.

evidence.title: Posterior sacroiliac fusion surgery: retrospective single-center study (LinQ and PsiF)
evidence.finding: VAS -3.6 cm from 9.5; 38.5% with >=50% improvement; zero procedure-related AEs; 26% withdrawal.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Omnia Medical (Morgantown, WV), private. The shift from the PsiF allograft to the 510(k) titanium PsiF DNA (transfixing, 27279-eligible) is the clearest example of a posterior vendor re-engineering around the 2025 LCDs.

new_record.challenge: Omnia's site does not describe the original PsiF implant's material; its allograft nature is taken from Kaye 2024 ('sacroiliac fusion allograft implants ... PsiF System from Omnia Medical') and Lynch 2022. Tissue bank and launch year not disclosed.

new_record.name: Vyrsa Pro cortical allograft (Vyrsa V1 titanium is the device)
new_record.company: Globus Medical (via Nevro, via Vyrsa Technologies)
new_record.composition: Custom cortical allograft implant for posterior SI joint fusion delivered through an 'inferior inlet' approach (Nevro acquisition release, Nov 2023). Vyrsa V1 (introduced end-2022) and Nevro1 (NCT06909292, 'SI transfixing and fusion system') are the titanium transfixing systems in the same portfolio.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical publication retrieved for Vyrsa Pro. Nevro's post-market study NCT06909292 (n=180, completed May 2025) covers the titanium Nevro1 transfixing system.
applications.caveats: Portfolio changed hands twice in 17 months (Vyrsa -> Nevro, 30 Nov 2023, $40M plus up to $35M milestones; Nevro -> Globus, closed 3 Apr 2025, ~$250M); current Globus branding and catalog status of the allograft not confirmed.

evidence.title: Post-market multicenter study of the Nevro1 SI transfixing and fusion system
evidence.finding: Completed May 2025; results not posted; titanium transfixing device, not the allograft.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Globus now owns both a lateral HA-coated screw line (SI-LOK/SI-LOK SELECT) and the Vyrsa posterior portfolio; Globus product pages name no graft brand for either, so the Osteocel-with-SI-LOK pairing in the brief is unverified.

new_record.ownership_history: Vyrsa Technologies (founded 2021) -> Nevro Corp (30 Nov 2023) -> Globus Medical (3 Apr 2025).
new_record.challenge: Vyrsa Pro's current availability under Globus, tissue bank and procedure volumes are not public.
